text.p: JULY Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
LIFFE coffee futures were seen getting "danger" signals and were expected to pull back from recent gains in the near term.
But July was still called to open between $20 and $30 higher after erasing early losses on Wednesday to close up at $2,090, near the session high.
New York coffee rallied even more strongly from negative territory. July soared 12.85 cents per lb, or more than five percent, to end at 253.10 cents.
Despite those sharp gains and strong closes, independent analyst Elli Gifford said she saw some "danger signals."
She noted that coffee remained extremely overbought and that slow stochastics were at higher levels and "tipping into the sell side."

"On balance, coffee will try to go higher, but it will be difficult," Gifford said. She pegged solid July robusta resistance at $2,200 and expected a test of strong support in the near-term at $1,950 to correct overbought signals.
